known_event.name: CPCB Daily AQI Bulletin 2024-11-18: Delhi Severe, prominent pollutant PM2.5 (36/39 stations)
known_event.source: https://cpcb.gov.in/upload/Downloads/AQI_Bulletin_20241118.pdf (retained probe/out/aqi_bulletin_20241118.pdf); the 90 ug/m3 edge is the Poor-band lower breakpoint of CPCB's own National AQI (About AQI PDF, probe/out/about_aqi.pdf, corroborated by AQI-Calculator.xlsx). Measured panel confirmation: 36/36 complete Delhi cpcb station-days on 2024-11-18 carry a 24-hr mean > 90 ug/m3 (235.7-731.5)

task.prediction_time: 23:59 IST on day D: every hourly reading through day D is knowable at that instant and no D+1 reading exists yet; features are the station's own trailing daily PM2.5 statistics through day D plus calendar terms and the station's coarse identity
task.target_definition: the station's D+1 calendar-day 24-hour mean PM2.5 exceeds 90 ug/m3 (strict >), the Poor-band lower breakpoint of CPCB's National AQI for 24-hour PM2.5; both the D and D+1 days must carry n_hours >= 18
task.description: for a CPCB CAAQMS station in India, predict whether the next calendar day's 24-hour mean PM2.5 is Poor-or-worse (> 90 ug/m3) from the station's own trailing daily history and the calendar

prediction_instant.citation: the instant is the end of day D in IST (the XKDR archive's collected_at is naive IST, UTC+05:30); the station's own hourly readings through day D are the administrative record. The archive republishes the publisher's measurements with no gap filling ('as reported', 'preliminary and not fully validated', XKDR README); intraday publication latency is unmeasured and day-D trailing completeness at the instant is an explicitly declared assumption

row_selection.basis: scored rows are complete (n_hours >= 18) station-days of the cpcb_caaqm PM2.5 stream with day D inside the declared window AND a labelable D+1 (a row present with n_hours >= 18). Day-D completeness is knowable at the instant; the D+1 observability rule is an outcome-observability exclusion that never reads the label value - unlabelable rows are excluded and counted per split. The 2025-04..09 partial tail (47,566 station-days, 829 valid-day positives) is excluded and counted; the 2025-01..03 and 2025-10..12 hole months are asserted empty. Both label values are retained in every window

evaluation_contract.scope_note: each row is one station-day next-day exceedance prediction at 23:59 IST on day D; features are precomputed at construction and the runner predicts row-wise from the shipped columns. Labeled eval is development/validation; the holdout is the final test and stays outside evaluated agents' workspaces. Training-label timing is UNVERIFIED: XKDR publishes a single cleaned export (no historical vintages, no first-publication ledger), so no full-row availability ledger can be constructed - retrospective research only, never a certified historical forecasting setup

vintage.evidence: the archive is one export stamped 2026-09-30T11:25:11+00:00 (/v1/meta, asserted by this build: exported_at and the 196,521,834-row count are pinned; a re-export refuses the build). Values are 'as reported' with 'no gap filling' and marked 'preliminary and not fully validated' (XKDR README); revision behaviour is unmeasured because a second export has never been observed. Every shipped feature is the current-vintage value of a measurement at or before day D; no as-of value is claimed

selection.evidence: membership is fixed by day-D completeness (n_hours >= 18, knowable at the instant) and the declared window; the only additional rule is D+1 outcome observability (a row with n_hours >= 18 must exist for D+1), which never reads the label value - unlabelable rows are excluded and counted per split. Positives are winter-clustered, so the day-level observability rule could in principle co-move with the label through weather (a monsoon D+1 is both thin and clean); the excluded counts per split and per month are recorded in summary.json so the exclusion's seasonality is measurable, not hidden

limitations: current_snapshot vintage: a single cleaned export, no historical vintages; values corrected after publication cannot be distinguished

the day-D trailing completeness assumption: CPCB intraday latency is unmeasured, so 23:59 IST features are declared under the assumption the day's hourly record is complete at the instant (the publisher's own 4 PM bulletin shows non-participating stations, so intraday availability is genuinely partial)

cross-row exposure: row D's label operand (the D+1 mean) ships as the pm25_mean feature of row D+1 and enters the trailing aggregates of rows D+2..D+91; the declared reverse-history probe measures the direct join exposure, access is isolated_rows, and the artifact is restricted retrospective research

outcome-observability selection: station-days whose D+1 is missing or thin are unlabelable and excluded (counted per split and per month); the exclusion is not label-reading but its seasonality is recorded
the export's 2025 hole (Jan-Mar, Oct-Dec absent) is why holdout is 2024, not 2025; the 2025-04..09 tail is excluded and counted
training_label_timing is unverified: no as-of ledger exists for when any daily aggregate first appeared in the archive
positives cluster by winter day and station; the independent positive evidence is the declared distinct-positive-days count, not the row count
labeled eval is development/validation, never an untouched final test; the holdout is the final test and remains sealed until the design is frozen

probes.name: next_day_mean_recovery
probes.note: blind-join label recovery: a donor row of the same station one day later donates its pm25_mean, which is exactly this row's label operand (the D+1 24-hr mean); gt 90 reproduces the label by construction. Coverage measures how many rows a same-station next-day join can answer outright on the full artifact

cross_row_audit.probes_note: the panel's serial structure is real and is measured, not argued away: row D's label is a function of the D+1 mean, which is row D+1's own pm25_mean feature, and the same value is inside the trailing aggregates of rows D+2..D+91 (the bounded-aggregate exposure is declared here; only the direct offset-1 join is exactly expressible as a probe). Coverage is expected to be high, which is why access is isolated_rows and the artifact is restricted retrospective research
cross_row_audit.rationale: rows are per-station next-day predictions whose trailing features are precomputed at construction; the runner predicts row-wise from shipped columns. The label source (the D+1 series) is absent from the shipped columns (asserted), but the same station's next row legitimately carries the outcome day as its own pm25_mean feature, so the cross-row join exposure is declared and measured rather than denied
cross_row_audit.auxiliary_files_review: the extract ships exactly the runner layout - public/train.csv, public/eval.csv, private/holdout.csv, meta.json, quality.json - plus summary.json, which carries fetch receipts, vintage pins, exclusion counts, per-window anchors and per-split per-month tables; no row-level source data and no performance metric. The fetched daily-aggregate lines stay in the job's scratch directory outside /output and are never uploaded
